title: Elastic entitlement bands + automated overage resolution (billing integration and acceptance criteria)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: customers with bursty token patterns need predictable soft-overage behavior and fewer manual invoices/credits after bursts. Current soft-burst model and static grace windows create costly manual reconciliations and surprise invoices.

Proposal summary: introduce 'Elastic Entitlement Bands' (EEBs) — per-plan, per-caller sliding windows that permit controlled temporary over-consumption with automated resolution and invoice-adjusted crediting. This feature combines runtime signals (rate-limit state, token consumption cadence) with billing automation so that short spikes are absorbed without ticketing, while sustained over-usage still produces predictable invoices.

Goals:
- Reduce manual crediting tickets by >= 60% for burst incidents.
- Provide transparent per-tenant UI and API signals about current band state and projected spend.
- Ensure reconciled billing ledger entries are explainable and match telemetry within 0.2% token variance.

Scope:
- API: entitlement query endpoints and usage webhooks.
- Console: entitlement band visualization, projected invoice preview, and auto-resolution toggles.
- Billing pipeline: invoice line item schema updates and auto-credit rules.
- Runtime: soft-overage enforcement policy that emits headers and events; no change to hard 429 enforcement.

Out of scope: meter redesign, SSO changes, new pricing tiers.

Stakeholders: PM (Aisha K.), Billing (Ravi Mendes), Runtime (Liam O'C.), Console Design (Marisol Vega), Legal/Finance (Theresa Liu).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Entitlement band semantics documented: each plan has baseline quota, an elastic band percentage (e.g., +20% for 1h), and a time-decay window. Docs must define exact decay math and examples.
AC-2: Runtime emits X-Redwood-Quota-State header with values OK | BAND_SOFT | BAND_EXCEEDED for every request when customer has EEBs enabled.
AC-3: Soft-overage behavior: when in BAND_SOFT the system should continue returning 200 but add X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining (tokens) and X-Redwood-Band-Expiry (ISO8601).
AC-4: Hard enforcement unchanged: once hard quota is exceeded and no fallback capacity exists, 429 is returned as today. EEBs do not convert hard limits to soft ones.

AC-5: Console presents current band usage, projected spend for remainder of billing window, and an "auto-resolve" toggle. Toggle default is ON for new trials and OFF for enterprise unless contract specifies otherwise.
AC-6: Billing pipeline: invoice line items include entitle_band_id, band_consumed_tokens, band_rate_per_token, and auto_credit_flag. Preview invoices must match runtime consumption within 0.2%.

AC-7: Auto-resolution: for consumptions within band that were later compensated by negative adjustments, the system must mark the invoice lines as "auto-resolved" and create a corresponding credit entry within 7 business days.
AC-8: Auditability: every auto-credit must have a linked justification event in the usage event log and be queryable via /v1/billing/adjustments?entitle_band_id=<id>.
AC-9: Admin ops: billing admins can manually override auto-resolution with reason codes; that action must create an incident entry and notify finance via webhook.

AC-10: Metrics: roll-out success criteria: 60% reduction in manual credit tickets related to short bursts within 90 days of launch, and <0.5% variance between telemetry and invoiced tokens at month-end.
AC-11: Security: entitle_band_id is not sensitive PII; access controls must restrict viewing to tenant-level admins and finance role. Security review sign-off required before release.
AC-12: Backfill behavior: for existing tenants with historical bursts older than 90 days, EEBs are not applied retroactively by default. Any backfill must be explicit and logged.
test_plan: TP-1: Unit tests for band decay math with deterministic timers and simulated token patterns (steady, spike, repeated spikes).

TP-2: Integration test where tenant consumes baseline + 15% spike for 45 minutes; verify header state becomes BAND_SOFT, console shows band expiry, and invoice preview includes band_consumed_tokens priced at band_rate_per_token.
TP-3: End-to-end billing test: synthetic tenant triggers auto-credit path; verify invoice line flagged auto-resolved and finance ledger balance updated in sandbox environment.
TP-4: Load test at 10k rps to ensure header emission adds <1ms p50 latency.
TP-5: Reconciliation test: compare telemetry tokens vs invoice tokens for 100 tenants across 30 days; assert <= 0.2% variance.
TP-6: Negative tests: verify that when band disabled at tenant level, the runtime returns existing behavior and no band headers are present.
rollout_plan: R-1: Feature-flag rollout. Stage 1: internal dogfood (2 internal tenants) for 2 weeks.
R-2: Stage 2: opt-in public beta for 50 customers selected across verticals for 4 weeks. Monitor metrics and support tickets daily.
R-3: Stage 3: auto-enable for trials; enterprise tenants must opt-in unless the contract mandates it. Gradual ramp to 20% of eligible tenants per week with canary metrics gating.
R-4: Full release gated on metrics and finance sign-off; provide billing migration runbook for finance ops.
notes: Design trade-off: showing projected spend requires conservative forecasting; design chooses percentile-based projection (75th percentile) and an explicit confidence indicator.
Accounting note: finance requires separate ledger account for band credits to avoid mixing with refunds; see finance doc (links below).
